gina_support: FYI — customer reports embeddings suddenly dropped from 1536 -> 1024 after they pinned a model variant. Search relevance broke. Ticket #3421, customer is asking for urgent help.
rafael_eng: Can you paste the exact API request/response they used? Also which model string did they pin (full pinned identifier if available)?
gina_support: They sent this snippet:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input": "hello world", "model": "redwood-embed-large-v2"}'
```Response (trimmed):```json
{
  "data": [ { "embedding": [0.001, -0.02, ... /* total 1024 values */ ] } ],
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v2"
}
```They say previously same call returned 1536-dim vectors.
ara_data: Quick checklist: did they re-index after the pinned upgrade? If index was built with 1536 vectors and queries now return 1024, that causes immediate break. Also ask them to run the model metadata endpoint to confirm what the platform reports for embedding_dim. Example: `GET /v1/models/redwood-embed-large-v2/metadata` should show embedding_dim.
ben_sre: I pulled routing logs for the customer's org_id — around the pinned rollout we have several capacity pressure fallbacks. It looks like requests for that model were routed to a cost-optimized variant labelled `redwood-embed-large-1024-quant` between 2026-03-10T02:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:15Z. That would explain the 1024 vectors.
gina_support: Do we have proof the pin actually pointed to the intended variant? Customer insists they pinned `redwood-embed-large-v2@pin-20260310-abc`.
deploy-bot: Rollout info for pin-20260310-abc: { id: "pin-20260310-abc", created_by: "acct_admin", created_at: "2026-03-10T01:58:03Z", routing_policy: "latency|fallback:cost-optimize-enabled" }
rafael_eng: Thanks — that routing policy is the giveaway. Pinning the logical model name doesn't prevent fallback if the pin is to a logical version and routing policies allow substitution for capacity/cost reasons. Two actionable next steps: 1) ask customer to call the model with the fully qualified pinned variant identifier (e.g., `model: "redwood-embed-large-v2@pin-20260310-abc"`) and return headers — specifically check `x-actual-model` or `x-model-variant` in the response; 2) confirm model metadata via `GET /v1/models/<variant>` and verify `embedding_dim`.
gina_support: I asked the customer to re-run with the explicit pinned variant and share headers. They returned:```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-model-variant: redwood-embed-large-1024-quant
content-type: application/json

{ "data": [ { "embedding": [ ... /* 1024 values */ ] } ] }
```So even when they called the pinned identifier it got routed to the 1024 variant.
ben_sre: That implies the pin was to the logical model version, and the platform applied variant substitution downstream. We need to check the pin resolution mapping. Rafael, can you check the resolution table for pin-20260310-abc?
rafael_eng: On it. Quick repro locally: calling `python` client with `model=\"redwood-embed-large-v2@pin-20260310-abc\"` returns 1024 dims for me too. Inspecting the model registry shows: `pin-20260310-abc -> logical:redwood-embed-large-v2 (aliases: [redwood-embed-large-1536-fp16, redwood-embed-large-1024-quant])` and an active substitution rule `fallback_to_cost_optimized=true`. That explains the behavior.
ara_data: For customer impact mitigation: 1) Recommend re-pinning to the explicit 1536 FP16 variant identifier (e.g., `redwood-embed-large-1536-fp16@rev-xxxxx`) so routing cannot substitute. 2) Re-ingest their index if vectors already changed. 3) We can also temporarily disable the fallback substitution for their org if they want.
gina_support: I proposed those options to the customer. They chose to pin to the explicit 1536 variant and reindex. Also asked us to disable org-level substitution until they're done.
ben_sre: I disabled fallback_to_cost_optimized for org_id in question at 2026-03-10T04:00Z. Monitor logs for any residual routing to 1024 variant; I added an alert if any response returns embedding length != 1536 for that org.
rafael_eng: Long-term: we should make pin semantics clearer in docs and add an API-level guard that returns a 409 if user requests pinned logical model but substitution would change embedding_dim. Filing follow-up GH issue.
gina_support: Customer acknowledged workaround and will reindex overnight. I'll keep ticket #3421 updated. :white_check_mark: 
rafael_eng: Thanks team — marking as high priority follow-up for model registry and docs.
